data.reason: Nothing has been produced. The ladder requires technical_spec, dev_plan, capability and implementation, and the spec comes first because the plan and the code both depend on it.
data.wave_reason: Technical_spec and capability are produced together because both can be written from the intent alone and neither needs the other to exist first. The capability states the observable contract (half the dots, limited time, score above a power pellet, once per game). The spec says how it is built. Dev_plan, stories and implementation wait because they need the spec's parts and flows. This fits the two-agent limit and leaves waves for dev_plan (with stories) and then implementation.

gap.statement: There is no technical design and no durable contract for the bonus fruit. Without them the work cannot be planned or built consistently: it is unclear where fruit state lives, how the half-dots trigger and the timer are measured, how the once-per-game rule is kept, and what score the fruit awards.

premises.text: The intent asks for a fruit that appears after half the dots are eaten, times out, scores more than a power pellet, and appears at most once per game. That behaviour is not yet specified technically or as a contract.
The ladder marks technical_spec and capability as required and missing, and nothing has been produced so far.

artifacts.task: Specify how the bonus fruit is built in the existing game. Cover the trigger at half the dots eaten, the fruit's position, its lifetime timer and expiry, the pacman collision and eating, the score value (strictly above a power pellet), the once-per-game guard, the state kept, the main flows, and how it is tested.

Write the durable capability contract for the bonus fruit, with criteria a test can check: it appears once half the dots are eaten, it disappears when its time runs out, eating it raises the score by more than a power pellet, and it appears at most once per game.

rejected.why: It needs the spec's parts and flows to sequence the work, so it waits for the spec.
Code before the spec and contract would invent the design and the criteria, so it waits.
The intent is already small and clear, and the quick-flow ladder does not require a brief or a prd.
Four required rungs are still missing, so no-move would be refused.
